headline: High: shared git/workspace and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between Aider and kotaemon.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo, while kotaemon processes documents and chat transcripts in a web UI. If kotaemon ingests Aider-authored files or transcripts as trusted content, injected instructions can cross the boundary. The pairwise pathway is plausible from documented surfaces, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF kotaemon ingests repo files or transcripts produced by Aider as authoritative instructions, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace without content provenance checks, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Restrict kotaemon to read-only copies of files
Add provenance labels to Aider-generated files
Disable automatic instruction-following from retrieved documents
Separate the shared git repo from kotaemon's document store
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider handles source code, git history, and API keys via env vars, and kotaemon touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys while calling external model APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from one agent into the other's prompts or uploads. The profiles document enough overlap to make leakage plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Aider and kotaemon share files or secrets in the same environment, sensitive code or keys can be exposed to both agents.
IF kotaemon sends retrieved documents to a third-party API, any Aider-written secrets in those documents may leak outward.
mitigations: Store API keys in separate secret scopes
Keep Aider and kotaemon in separate directories
Redact secrets before indexing documents
Limit kotaemon ingestion to non-sensitive corpora
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can execute shell commands, write the filesystem, and modify git state; kotaemon also has file access and broad network egress. Aider's shared git-repo state plus kotaemon's file-backed app data create a realistic write-write conflict on shared mutable resources, and git changes can be overwritten or misapplied without locking. This is dangerous in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or shared directory, concurrent writes can clobber each other's state.
IF kotaemon persists app data while Aider rewrites tracked files, race conditions can corrupt work products.
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Serialize access with a lock file
Disable concurrent writes to the same repo
Run one agent in read-only mode
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code changes and git commits, while kotaemon is a document/chat-centric system that can surface retrieved content to users or downstream workflows. If kotaemon treats Aider output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade from generated code or summaries into further actions. The interaction is inferred from documented roles, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF kotaemon uses Aider-generated text as source material without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Aider commits changes that kotaemon later summarizes or routes to users, mistakes can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Aider output
Add verification steps in kotaemon retrieval pipelines
Mark Aider outputs as untrusted until checked
Limit automated downstream actions from summaries
requires-engineering: implement citation and provenance validation

E_compliance.rationale: Aider touches source code, git history, and API keys, while kotaemon handles documents, PDFs, chat transcripts, and API keys. If regulated or sensitive documents are indexed into kotaemon and Aider can access the same workspace, retention and residency controls may diverge across the pair. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are placed in kotaemon's corpus and Aider can read the same files, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF the two agents retain logs or transcripts under different policies, deletion and retention requests may not propagate consistently.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Separate retention policies per agent
Document which agent stores which data class
Purge transcripts and caches after use
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows
